title: Animals Everywhere
keyIdea: Animals live all over the world — on land, in water and in the air — and every continent, even icy Antarctica, is home to animals suited to the conditions where they live.
familyTip: Look at a globe or world map. Point to a forest, an ocean, a desert and Antarctica. Name one animal for each (parrot, whale, camel, penguin) and say land, water or air.

visual.caption: Animals everywhere — fair idea or myth? Drag each clue, or tap it and then tap a box.

lab.caption: Flagship lab: place fish in water, confirm Antarctica has penguins, match camel to desert, reject polar-bear-in-desert and only-near-me myths, then challenge.

kid: Animals live on land. They also live in water. Some fly in the air.
Every big land has animals. Even cold Antarctica has penguins.
A camel fits a hot dry desert. A whale fits the ocean. A parrot fits the trees.
Animals are not only near your house. They are not only in zoos. They live all over the world.
adult: This is early science about living things and where they live. Animals use land, water and air. They live on every continent. Key words: continent, habitat, suit, desert, ocean, forest, Antarctica. A child should name animals from different places and say if each uses land, water or air.
Common mistakes: thinking Antarctica has no animals; putting a polar bear in a desert; thinking animals live only near home or only in zoos; forgetting that birds use the air.

In the lab, your child puts a fish in water, says yes to penguins in Antarctica, matches a camel to desert, says no to a polar bear in a desert, and rejects the only-near-me idea. The challenge traps those slips.

practice.hint: Think of fins and gills — what kind of place fits?
practice.explain: Fish live in water. Fins and gills fit wet places, not dry land or clouds.

choices: only has animals in zoos far away
practice.explain: Antarctica is icy and still home to animals such as penguins — it is not empty.

practice.prompt: You name {n} animals from different places. {k} of them live in water. How many do not live in water?
practice.hint: Start with all the animals you named, then take away the water ones.
practice.explain: You named {n} animals and {k} live in water, so {=n-k} do not.

practice.prompt: A map shows {a} habitats on land and {b} habitats in water. How many habitats is that altogether?
practice.hint: Add the land habitats and the water habitats.
practice.explain: {a} land habitats and {b} water habitats make {=a+b} habitats altogether.

practice.explain: Animals use land, water and air on every continent, each suited to its place.
